title: rwb-integration ACE plan status: the login, the account resolution, the interface field types, the meaning of live and messageCode, the two settings, the connection-matrix rows and the ownership split are not settled by any one source
source: WP B-P2-01; legacy RWB-E2-002; Ownership Map v1 (GET /cases/{caseId}/plan-status owner P2; interface_config, outbound_item, job_catalog owner P2; lov_value, reference_row, parameter_catalog, parameter_value owner P3; rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row, decision_log_entry owner P7); API Specification v4 /cases/{caseId}/plan-status and the PlanStatus schema; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 8, 9, 11, 13, 14, 16, 24, 29, 37, 41, 43, 44 and 45; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md slides 11, 12, 14 and 27; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P2 Integration v3.md (scope and REQ-DRI-013); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P2 Integration v3.md T1.1 and T-A.2 API-P2-010; RWB-P3-E2002-APP; RWB-ITG-E2002-ITG
description: One combined gap covers what this slice cannot read from a single source. (1) The rwb-integration login name (DP-02) is given nowhere; the legacy story ran on the shared recovery service identity. (2) The account numbers of the case: the operation is case-scoped and takes the case reference only, while the ACE interface is keyed by account number, so the accounts have to be read first; no source states that the read calls the rwb-case case read, and the work package's contract row names only the parameters, reference-data and rule-catalog contracts. (3) The field types, lengths, required flags, null rules and query shapes of the case read, of the reference-data and parameter answers, of the authorise answer and of the remaining RestructurePlanQuery elements are given nowhere; only the four plan element names are. (4) The meaning of live and messageCode is split across sources: the API Specification carries both fields, the legacy story says live is true when read from ACE now, and neither says who fills the message when the live read fails; the case side needs the flag to choose between the two answers. (5) The two settings rwb.ace.plan.batch-size = 500 and rwb.ace.plan.timeout-ms = 2000 are legacy properties recorded as an assumption under DL11, while DP-06 makes parameters rwb-case data; no source states which owner carries them or how they are read. (6) The connection matrix gives P2 no row to ACE Common and no row to P3, and no row from P3 to P2, although the interface call, the account resolution and the daily call all exist; the omission is a defect of the matrix, not of the design. (7) The ownership split is fixed only by the plan and the Ownership Map: the ACE read and the live answer here, the stored status, the compare, the route state, the rules, the task, the timer, the decision record and the panel in rwb-case, the rights in rwb-access and the package in rwb-decision. (8) The routing of the daily call: the sibling story makes the plan-status step a step of JOB-02 owned by rwb-case, the integration harness lists a plan-status step on rwb-integration, and the job map gives JOB-02 to rwb-case; the sibling and the job map agree and the harness row is the outlier. (9) The stored fallback: the legacy story answers the stored status from the same endpoint, the target splits it into the rwb-case stored answer and this live answer, and the composite route that merges them has no published path or merge order.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-002 section 4 step 2 (the case list with account numbers through the P3 CaseQuery), step 3 (statusFor in batches of 500, assumed; DL11), step 8 (the endpoint reads ACE live with a 2-second timeout and falls back to the stored status) and section 12 (PlanStatus: planRef, status, statusDate, live, messageCode; RestructurePlanQuery.statusFor returning planRef, accountNo, status, statusDate); section 13 (properties rwb.ace.plan.batch-size and rwb.ace.plan.timeout-ms, assumed; DL11) and section 17 (no read of another module's tables, ACE data only through the interface). API Specification v4 /cases/{caseId}/plan-status x-module P2, x-capability Case record R, operationId getCasesCaseidPlanStatus, and the PlanStatus schema with planRef, status, statusDate, live and messageCode and no accountNo. TSD P2 v3 T1.1 (v_ace_plan tier 1, API-P2-010) and T-A.2 API-P2-010 (read from v_ace_plan with fallback to plan_status and plan_status_as_of). Arch v5 slide 13 (P2 row: P5 REST and Outside file only; no cell to ACE Common and no cell from P3 to P2), slide 16 (P2 IN GET /interface-runs and POST /interface-runs/{id}/retry, OUT FileDelivered and FileFailed), slide 41 (rwb_integration owns interface config, file runs, outbound items, ACE integration paths), slide 44 (JOB-02 owner rwb-case, mechanism AceDataReady to DailyCaseRun), slide 45 (only rwb-source-data reads the thirty views) and slide 11 (OpenAPI 3.1, one hop, 2 s). RWB-P3-E2002-APP section 4 step 3 (the readPlanStatus activity calls the P2 operation one case per call) and section 12.2. RWB-ITG-E2002-ITG section 12.5 (plan-status step on rwb-integration). No source names the login, the case-read call of this slice, the consumed field types, the messageCode owner, the owner of the two settings or the composite route.
proposed: Settle in the wave 2 contract review: the rwb-integration login with the ACE DB owner; the case read this slice consumes and its contract story; the field sets of the case read, the reference answers, the authorise answer and the remaining interface elements; the owner of live and messageCode with the composite route's merge rule; the owner and read path of the two settings; the P2-to-ACE-Common and P3-to-P2 rows of the connection matrix; and one daily step, in rwb-case. Record the outcome in RWB-P2-E2002-CON, RWB-P2-E2002-OPS, RWB-P3-E2002-APP and the registers; no business value changes in this story.

title: The plan-status contract baseline: the accountNo field, the meaning and owner of live and messageCode, the interface null rules, the consumed read shapes, the composite route and the two specification conflicts are not fixed by any one source
source: WP B-P2-01; legacy RWB-E2-002; Ownership Map v1 (GET /cases/{caseId}/plan-status owner P2, basis API Specification v4 and TSD v5 P2 appendix T-A); API Specification v4 /cases/{caseId}/plan-status, the PlanStatus schema and x-capability Case record R; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 10, 11, 12, 13, 16, 41, 43, 44 and 45; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md slides 11 and 27; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P2 Integration v3.md T1.1 and T-A.2 API-P2-010; RWB-P3-E2002-APP; RWB-ITG-E2002-ITG
description: One combined gap covers the six things a contract cannot be faked without. (1) The answer shape: the API Specification PlanStatus carries planRef, status, statusDate, live and messageCode and no accountNo, while the legacy interface answer carries accountNo and the sibling case story joins on it; this contract adds the field and nothing in the source set settles whether it belongs in the resource. (2) The two flag fields: live and messageCode have a type and no rule; the legacy story says live is true when read from ACE now, the sibling story answers live false with MSG-P2-008 and the stored date, and no source says which provider fills the message, so the two-provider resource has no agreed rule. (3) The interface: the legacy story publishes the statusFor signature and four element names, and nothing about the null rules, the empty answer, the error classes, the batch boundary or the retry, all of which the app story has to implement. (4) The consumed reads: the case read, the authorise answer and the two reference answers have no paths, no element names and no types in any source; the reference-data and parameter contracts are named by DP-07 and DP-06 and their shapes are pending. (5) The composite route: the case record plan section is composed at the edge from this answer and the stored answer of rwb-case, and no source gives the route path, the merge order or the field precedence. (6) The two specification conflicts: the Technical Specification reads v_ace_plan with a fallback to the case columns, which ADR-010, DP-05 and the view rule refuse, and the Ownership Map and the API Specification keep the operation with P2 while the base changes to the integration base; both are reconciled here and recorded, not silently applied.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-002 section 12 (the endpoint row: PlanStatus planRef, status, statusDate, live; the published interfaces with RestructurePlanQuery.statusFor(List<String>) returning planRef, accountNo, status, statusDate; the errors 401, 403, 404 and the authorization Case record R; read only, writes nothing) and section 4 step 8. API Specification v4 /cases/{caseId}/plan-status (x-module P2, x-capability Case record R, operationId getCasesCaseidPlanStatus, errors 401, 403, 404, 503) and the PlanStatus schema (planRef, status, statusDate, live, messageCode). TSD P2 v3 T1.1 (v_ace_plan tier 1, API-P2-010) and T-A.2 API-P2-010 (read from v_ace_plan with fallback to plan_status and plan_status_as_of; errors 401, 403, 404, 503; Idempotency not applicable). Arch v5 slide 13 (P2 row: no cell to ACE Common, no cell from P3 to P2), slide 16 (P2 IN and OUT contract), slide 41 (rwb_integration and the base), slide 44 (JOB-02 owner rwb-case) and slide 45 (only rwb-source-data reads the views). RWB-P3-E2002-APP section 12.1 (the stored answer on the rwb-case base, live false and MSG-P2-008) and RWB-ITG-E2002-ITG section 12.5 (a plan-status step listed on rwb-integration).
proposed: Approve the four assumptions of RWB-P2-E2002-CON at the contract review before the baseline is tagged: the answer shape with accountNo, the live and messageCode rule on a two-provider resource, the interface contract with its batch, budget and answer rules, and the consumed read shapes with the composite route. Reconcile the interface-versus-view wording of the technical specification in the Service Contract Catalog, and record the re-basing of the operation on the integration base.

title: The plan-status deployment values, the ACE endpoint and certificate references, the two setting values at run time, the trigger wiring, the alert thresholds, the mapping of the no-package condition and the fixture owner are not fixed in the source documents
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 11, 16, 20, 24, 33, 41, 44 and 45; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md slides 11, 12 and 27; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (rulings on interface_config, job_catalog, parameter_catalog, reference_row and feature_flag); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P2 Integration v3.md T1.1, T7 and T-A.2 API-P2-010; ADR-023; RWB-P2-E2002-CON; RWB-P2-E2002-APP
description: The deployment needs nine values or rules that no source fixes. (1) The rwb-integration identity name and its secret reference are not stated; only DP-02 states that one login per service exists. (2) The ACE common module endpoint, its certificate, its network path and its per-environment availability are not in any source, and the interface is not an interface_config row, so the release has no table to read them from. (3) The two settings have no stated run-time owner: the legacy story records them as service properties under DL11, DP-06 makes parameters rwb-case data, and the deployment has to know which of the two wins in an environment. (4) The budget rule is not stated: the operation must refuse inside the caller's 2 s budget, so a timeout value longer than the budget is a release defect, and no source gives the margin. (5) The trigger wiring is not written down: the calling paths are the rwb-case activity and the composite route, no P2 Schedule exists, and the integration harness nevertheless lists a plan-status step on rwb-integration. (6) The alert thresholds of the unavailable rate, the refusal rates, the unknown-status count and the duration against the budget are not stated, and the platform alert catalogue carries message identifiers, not values. (7) The no-package-in-force condition has no home here: this service never evaluates a package, so no series, alert or runbook entry of this release can observe it, and the mapping has to name its owners instead. (8) The dashboard dimensions, the retention of the series, the replica counts, the resource sizes and the probe timings have no baseline. (9) The owner of the synthetic fixtures of the smoke run is not stated.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 16 (P2 IN GET /interface-runs and POST /interface-runs/{id}/retry, OUT FileDelivered and FileFailed, with no ACE Common cell in the row) and slide 41 (schema rwb_integration, base /api/recovery/integration/v1, topic and task queue); slide 44 (JOB-02 owner rwb-case, no plan-status job for P2); slide 45 (only rwb-source-data reads the views); slide 24 and the Temporal and Drools design slide 11 (namespace, task queue, worker versioning as capabilities); slide 11 (OpenAPI 3.1, one hop, 2 s). TSD P2 v3 T1.1 (v_ace_plan tier 1) and T-A.2 API-P2-010 (no operational value), T7 (NFR targets with no numbers). The ownership rulings record job_catalog and interface_config as P2 tables and parameter and reference data as P3, and feature_flag as a platform library object. ADR-023 requires observability per service and gives no threshold. RWB-ITG-E2002-ITG section 12.5 lists a plan-status step on rwb-integration, which the job map and RWB-P3-E2002-APP contradict.
proposed: Approve the three assumptions of RWB-P2-E2002-OPS in the release readiness review: the identity and environment values with no Schedule and no migration, the trigger wiring with the ACE-or-stub record and the corrected harness row, and the five series, four alerts, the named no-package row and the four runbook entries. Carry every threshold and endpoint as an environment value and never as code.
